package_info.why_malicious: The application masquerades as a legitimate COVID-19 tracking app but contains ransomware functionality. Upon installation and launch, it requests device administrator privileges, then forcefully changes the device's lock screen password and displays a ransom note overlay, denying user access to the device until a ransom is paid. This behavior constitutes device-locking ransomware and is a severe security threat.

execution_context.trigger: After app installation and initial launch, upon granting device admin privileges
execution_context.file_location: Covid19 Tracker Android APK, main activity code (e.g., MainActivity.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After app installation and initial launch, the code requests device administrator privileges, then programmatically changes the device's lock screen password to a randomly generated value and displays a ransom note overlay on top of all other apps, resulting in denial of user access to the device until a ransom is paid.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code forcefully changes the device's lock screen password and displays a ransom note overlay without user consent, which is a hallmark of ransomware. This action immediately locks the user out of their own device and demands payment for restoration of access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate COVID-19 tracking app should never request device administrator privileges to alter security settings, change the device password, or restrict user access. Such actions are not required for any legitimate tracking or informational functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise device management apps may change device passwords, but only with explicit user or administrator consent and within managed environments. In those cases, users are informed and can opt out; here, the action is performed without consent and for extortion.
key_indicators: Request for device administrator privileges during or immediately after installation
Programmatic change of device lock screen password without user initiation
Display of persistent ransom note overlay preventing normal device use
Immediate denial of user access to device following app launch

attack_chain.action: User is lured to a phishing site (coronavirusapp[.]site) and downloads the malicious APK.
User installs the Covid19 Tracker app and is prompted to grant device administrator privileges.
attack_chain.leads_to: App gains elevated permissions required for malicious actions

attack_chain.action: User launches the Covid19 Tracker app, which executes code to change the device password and lock the screen.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is denied access to the device

attack_chain.action: App displays a ransom note overlay demanding payment to unlock the device.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: extortion of ransom payment

behavioral_signatures: Android application requests device administrator privileges immediately after installation
App programmatically changes device lock screen password without user initiation
Display of persistent ransom note overlay after app launch
Sudden denial of device access following installation of a new app
file_indicators: APK files named 'Covid19 Tracker', 'CovidLock', or similar COVID-19 themed names
App manifest requesting android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and device admin privileges
Presence of ransom note resources or strings within the APK
network_indicators: Distribution from coronavirusapp[.]site or other COVID-19 themed phishing domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request device administrator privileges and attempt to change the device password immediately after installation, especially if distributed from unofficial sources or COVID-19 themed domains. Detect overlays displaying ransom notes and sudden loss of device access following installation of new apps. Scan APKs for ransom note resources and analyze app manifests for SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and device admin requests.
